faqs.q: Is a React Native app as good as a native app?
faqs.a: For most business apps, yes: users get smooth screens and native controls. If your app depends on heavy graphics or specialised device features, we tell you early and may recommend native code for those parts or a fully native build.

faqs.q: How is React Native different from Flutter?
faqs.a: Both build iOS and Android apps from one codebase. React Native uses JavaScript and native interface components, which suits teams that already work with web technologies. Flutter draws its own interface, which suits highly custom designs. We help you choose based on your app and your team.

faqs.q: Can you add features to our existing React Native app?
faqs.a: Yes. We start with a review of the code, dependencies and store setup, then plan fixes and new features in sprints.

faqs.q: Can the app share code with our website?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Business logic and some components can be shared with a React web app, which keeps features aligned and reduces upkeep.

faqs.q: What happens after launch?
faqs.a: We stay for updates, new iOS and Android versions, bug fixes, performance tuning and new features, with simple reports.

faqs.q: Why choose Flutter for our app?
faqs.a: Flutter is a strong fit when design matters and you want iOS and Android from one build. It draws its own interface, so screens look and behave the same everywhere, and one team maintains one codebase.

faqs.q: Flutter or React Native: which should we pick?
faqs.a: Both are proven for business apps. Flutter suits highly custom, animated designs; React Native suits teams that already use JavaScript or want to share code with a React website. We compare both against your app in plain language.

faqs.q: Can a Flutter app use the camera, GPS and other phone features?
faqs.a: Yes, through well-supported plugins, with native code for anything specialised.

faqs.q: Can you take over an existing Flutter app?
faqs.a: Yes. We review the code, packages and store setup, fix what's urgent first, then plan new features in sprints.

faqs.q: Can a Flutter app also run in the browser?
faqs.a: Flutter can target the web too. For public, content-heavy sites a regular website is usually better, but for internal tools and dashboards a Flutter web build can share most of the app's code.

faqs.q: What is cross-platform app development?
faqs.a: Building one app that runs on iOS, Android and often the web from a shared codebase, instead of separate apps for each platform.

faqs.q: Will a cross-platform app feel slower than a native one?
faqs.a: For most business apps, users won't notice a difference. Apps with heavy graphics or specialised device features may need native parts, and we flag that during the first call.

faqs.q: When is a native app the better choice?
faqs.a: If you need top performance or heavy device features, go native. If you need iOS and Android fast on one budget, cross-platform is usually the better fit.

faqs.q: Can we add a web version later?
faqs.a: Yes. We structure the code so business logic and components can be shared with a web app when you're ready.

faqs.q: Does cross-platform development cost less?
faqs.a: Usually, because one team builds and maintains one codebase instead of two or three. The saving depends on how much platform-specific work your app needs, and we show it in your estimate.

faqs.q: What is a progressive web app?
faqs.a: A web app that behaves like a mobile app: it can be added to the home screen, opens full screen, works offline and can send notifications, without an app store download.

faqs.q: Do we need a PWA or a native app?
faqs.a: A PWA works well when a browser app is enough and installation shouldn't be required. If you need heavy device features or top performance, a native or cross-platform app is the better fit, and we help you decide.

faqs.q: Do progressive web apps work on iPhones?
faqs.a: Yes. Users can add a PWA to the home screen from Safari, and recent iOS versions support notifications for installed web apps. Some device features are more limited than in native apps, so we check these against your needs first.

faqs.q: Can a PWA be listed in the app stores?
faqs.a: It can be published on Google Play, and on the App Store with a native wrapper, subject to Apple's review rules. Many teams don't need store listings at all, since users install straight from the browser.

faqs.q: Will it work for users with poor internet?
faqs.a: Yes. That's one of the main reasons to choose a PWA: cached screens load quickly, key features work offline, and data syncs when the connection returns.
